steps.tx: **Dyslipidaemia** (abnormal blood lipid levels) is defined by raised **low density lipoprotein cholesterol** (LDL cholesterol, the artery clogging cholesterol type), raised triglycerides or low high density lipoprotein cholesterol. **Primary prevention** (treating risk before any event) uses total cardiovascular risk scores such as SCORE2 to set treatment intensity. **Hypertriglyceridaemia** (raised triglycerides above one point seven millimoles per litre) adds pancreatitis risk when severe.
steps.say: Dyslipidaemia is abnormal blood lipid levels. It includes raised low density lipoprotein cholesterol raised triglycerides or low high density lipoprotein cholesterol. Primary prevention can treat risk before any event and it uses total cardiovascular risk scores such as SCORE two. Raised triglycerides above one point seven millimoles per litre add pancreatitis risk when severe.

steps.tx: **Lipoproteins** (fat carriers in blood) include **chylomicrons** (dietary fat carriers), **very low density lipoprotein** (liver fat exporter), low density lipoprotein and high density lipoprotein which scavenges cholesterol. **Lipoprotein(a)** (genetically raised particle) confers risk independent of LDL cholesterol and is measured once in a lifetime. **Apolipoprotein B** (particle number marker) captures remnant risk better than LDL cholesterol alone.
steps.say: Lipoproteins are fat carriers in blood. Chylomicrons can carry dietary fat while very low density lipoprotein exports liver fat. Low density lipoprotein can carry cholesterol to arteries and high density lipoprotein can scavenge cholesterol. Lipoprotein small a is a genetically raised particle measured once in a lifetime and apolipoprotein B captures particle number better than LDL cholesterol.

steps.tx: **Familial hypercholesterolaemia** (FH, genetic LDL receptor defect causing lifelong high LDL) presents with premature coronary disease and tendon xanthomas, while **secondary causes** include hypothyroidism, nephrotic syndrome, cholestasis and drugs such as steroids. **Insulin resistance** (impaired insulin action) drives high triglycerides with low high density lipoprotein in metabolic syndrome. **Smoking and diabetes** amplify vascular injury from any given LDL level.
steps.say: Familial hypercholesterolaemia means a genetic LDL receptor defect causing lifelong high LDL with premature coronary disease. Secondary causes include hypothyroidism nephrotic syndrome cholestasis and steroids. Insulin resistance can drive high triglycerides with low high density lipoprotein in metabolic syndrome. Smoking and diabetes amplify vascular injury from any given LDL level.

steps.tx: **Atherosclerosis** (cholesterol plaque build up) begins with endothelial injury and apolipoprotein B particle retention in the intima. **Inflammation** (immune cell recruitment and foam cell formation) enlarges the plaque and thins its fibrous cap. **Plaque rupture** (cap tear with thrombosis) causes most acute events, which is why lifetime LDL exposure matters more than a single recent value.
steps.say: Atherosclerosis can begin with endothelial injury and apolipoprotein B particle retention in the artery wall. Inflammation can recruit immune cells and foam cells which enlarge plaque and thin its fibrous cap. Plaque rupture with thrombosis causes most acute events. Lifetime LDL exposure therefore can matter more than a single recent value.

steps.tx: **Tendon xanthoma** (cholesterol nodule in Achilles or hand tendons) and **xanthelasma** (yellow eyelid cholesterol deposit) point toward familial disease, while **corneal arcus** (grey corneal ring before age forty five) supports severe hypercholesterolaemia. **Eruptive xanthoma** (yellow papules) signals very high triglycerides. **Peripheral arterial disease** (calf pain on walking) and coronary events in young patients raise suspicion for high cumulative LDL burden.
steps.say: Tendon xanthoma is a cholesterol nodule in Achilles or hand tendons and it points toward familial disease. Xanthelasma is yellow eyelid cholesterol deposit and corneal arcus is a grey corneal ring before age forty five. Eruptive xanthomas can signal very high triglycerides. Peripheral arterial disease with young coronary events can raise suspicion for high cumulative LDL burden.

steps.tx: **Fasting lipid profile** (nonfasting sample is acceptable) is the first test giving total cholesterol, LDL cholesterol, high density lipoprotein cholesterol and triglycerides, while **non high density lipoprotein cholesterol** (all atherogenic cholesterol) is calculated as total minus high density value. **Dutch Lipid Clinic Criteria** (FH scoring system from family history, clinical signs, LDL level and DNA) stratify suspected familial disease. **Liver function tests** precede statin therapy to establish baseline.
steps.say: Fasting lipid profile is the first test giving total cholesterol LDL cholesterol high density cholesterol and triglycerides. Non high density cholesterol means all atherogenic cholesterol and it is calculated as total minus high density value. Dutch Lipid Clinic Criteria stratify suspected familial hypercholesterolaemia from family history signs LDL level and DNA. Liver function tests should precede statin therapy.

steps.tx: **High intensity statin** (atorvastatin seventy five to eighty milligrams) is first line for secondary prevention and high risk primary prevention because it lowers LDL by at least fifty percent. **Ezetimibe** (cholesterol absorption blocker) is added when LDL remains above target despite maximal statin, while **PCSK9 inhibitor** (monoclonal antibody freeing LDL receptors) suits familial disease or very high risk patients. **Icosapent ethyl** (purified fish oil ester) reduces events in high triglyceride patients on statins.
steps.say: High intensity statin such as atorvastatin seventy five to eighty milligrams is first line for secondary prevention. It can lower LDL by at least fifty percent. Ezetimibe blocks absorption and it is added when LDL remains above target despite maximal statin. PCSK nine inhibitor can free LDL receptors and it suits familial disease or very high risk patients.

steps.tx: **European Society of Cardiology** targets low density lipoprotein below fifty five milligrams per decilitre for very high risk and below one hundred milligrams per decilitre for high risk, with at least fifty percent reduction from baseline. **American College of Cardiology** uses a threshold of seventy milligrams per decilitre for adding ezetimibe or PCSK9 inhibitor in very high risk patients. **Risk enhancers** (family history, lipoprotein small a, chronic kidney disease) lower the threshold for early therapy.
steps.say: European Society of Cardiology should target low density lipoprotein below fifty five milligrams per decilitre for very high risk. High risk target sits below one hundred milligrams per decilitre with at least fifty percent reduction from baseline. American College of Cardiology uses seventy milligrams per decilitre for adding ezetimibe or PCSK nine inhibitor. Risk enhancers can lower the threshold for early therapy.

steps.tx: **Myopathy** (muscle pain and weakness) and **rhabdomyolysis** (muscle breakdown with myoglobinuria) are the feared statin adverse effects, while **baseline creatine kinase** (CK, muscle enzyme) is checked only when symptoms appear. **Transaminase rise** (liver enzyme elevation) above three times normal warrants repeat testing rather than automatic discontinuation. **New diabetes** (impaired glucose tolerance) risk rises slightly with intensive statins but cardiovascular benefit dominates decisively.
steps.say: Myopathy is muscle pain and weakness and rhabdomyolysis is muscle breakdown with myoglobin in urine. Baseline creatine kinase is checked only when symptoms appear. Transaminase rise above three times normal warrants repeat testing rather than automatic discontinuation. New diabetes risk rises slightly with intensive statins but cardiovascular benefit dominates.

steps.tx: **Familial screening** (cascade testing of first degree relatives of definite FH patients) finds affected members before events occur, while **triglyceride above five hundred milligrams per decilitre** (severe elevation) needs fibrate plus insulin when pancreatitis threatens. **No stopping statin for pregnancy plans** without specialist advice is needed because familial disease carries high lifetime risk. **Cholesterol crystals** in tendon xanthomas rarely regress even when LDL falls, marking cumulative exposure.
steps.say: Cascade screening tests first degree relatives of definite familial hypercholesterolaemia patients before events occur. Triglycerides above five hundred milligrams per decilitre need fibrate and sometimes insulin when pancreatitis threatens. You should plan statin continuation around pregnancy with specialist advice because familial disease carries high lifetime risk. Tendon xanthomas can rarely regress even when LDL falls.

steps.tx: High-yield for the exam keeps targets, drug sequence and genetic clues together. First-line drug is **high intensity statin** giving at least fifty percent LDL reduction. Second line adds **ezetimibe**, then **PCSK9 inhibitor** for very high risk. Gold-standard confirmation for familial disease is genetic testing within **Dutch Lipid Clinic Criteria**. Numbers to quote are **fifty five**, **one hundred** and **seventy** milligrams per decilitre plus **lipoprotein small a measured once**.
steps.say: High yield revision can link targets drug sequence and genetic clues for dyslipidaemia. First line drug is high intensity statin giving at least fifty percent LDL reduction. Ezetimibe can add next and PCSK nine inhibitor can follow for very high risk. Dutch Lipid Clinic Criteria stratify familial disease with genetic testing as confirmation.
